explain.say: That cell divides into two, then four, then eight, making a ball of cells. Soon the cells begin to specialise: different genes switch on in different cells, so some become nerve, some muscle, some blood.

explain.say: After that the baby mostly grows bigger and its organs mature. About 38 weeks after fertilisation it is around 50 centimetres long and made of trillions of cells.

faq.q: How does a baby start from one cell?
faq.a: A baby begins as a fertilised egg: one cell carrying half its DNA from each parent. That cell divides over and over, and the new cells specialise to build the whole body.
asks: How big is the first cell of a baby?

faq.q: How do cells know what to become?
faq.a: Every cell has the same DNA, but signals from neighbouring cells switch different genes on or off. The genes that are switched on decide whether a cell becomes skin, nerve, muscle or something else.
asks: What makes a cell turn into a nerve cell?

faq.q: When does a baby's heart start beating?
faq.a: A simple tube-shaped heart starts beating about three weeks after fertilisation, when the embryo is only a few millimetres long. It later folds into a four-chambered heart.
asks: How early does the heart beat?

faq.q: What is the difference between an embryo and a fetus?
faq.a: For the first eight weeks after fertilisation the developing baby is called an embryo, while its main organs form. From then until birth it is called a fetus, and it mainly grows and matures.
asks: When does an embryo become a fetus?

faq.q: How big is a baby at birth?
faq.a: A newborn is usually about 50 centimetres long and weighs around 3 to 3.5 kilograms, grown from a single cell in about nine months.
asks: How long is a newborn baby?
How much does a baby grow before birth?

facts: A human egg cell is about 0.1 millimetres across, one of the largest cells in the body.
The heart tube begins beating about three weeks after fertilisation.
A developing baby is called an embryo for the first eight weeks and a fetus after that.

quiz.say: All of a baby's cells have the same DNA. Why do they become different kinds of cell?
quiz.show: Cells with the same DNA become different because…

options.show: Different genes are switched on in each kind
options.say: Different genes are switched on in each kind

quiz.why: Signals switch particular genes on or off, so cells with identical DNA end up doing different jobs.

wrong.1: Almost all body cells carry the same DNA.
wrong.2: Cells respond to signals, not by copying shapes.
